evidence.source: Shuowen.org, received Shuowen entry with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: definition; component analysis; sound note; borrowing discussion
evidence.text: The entry glosses 医 as a container for bows, crossbows, and arrows and analyzes it 从匸从矢. Duan’s commentary identifies the analysis as associative, reports 小徐’s additional 矢亦聲 sound analysis, and says the received Guoyu text has 翳 where the quoted passage has 医. This is historical lexicographic testimony; it does not independently establish an early artifact form or the depicted container’s name and pronunciation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「医」 - 「說文解字」在線查詢

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: Shuowen analysis; readings; senses of 殹
evidence.text: The entry reports 殹 as 从殳、医聲, gives Mandarin readings yì and yī, and records a sense of a sound associated with illness as well as grammatical-particle uses. This supports the dictionary’s account of 医 as a sound element within 殹. It does not settle the origin or depicted referent of 医, nor establish a historical sound change from its modern reading.
evidence.title: [C05910] 殹 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: form relationship; historical use of 医 for 醫
evidence.text: The 醫 entry lists 医 as a variant and cites Song–Yuan vulgar-character materials and a comparison of simplified-character tables stating 醫 is written 医. This supports the traditional 醫 → standardized simplified 医 relationship while leaving 医’s earlier graphic history separate and unresolved.
evidence.title: [A04248-022] 医 (醫) - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The 醫 record indexes the Guangyun fanqie 於其切 and 於其切 at the related phonological source. This is dictionary evidence for the traditional character’s historical reading tradition, not proof of a sound role for 矢 in 医.

evidence.text: The official Taiwan character record identifies 矢 as U+77E2 and gives its Mandarin reading shǐ. The local Baxter–Sagart row supplied in the dossier is distinct evidence: MC syijX and OC *l̥i[j]ʔ, gloss ‘arrow’; no exact B–S reading for 医 is supplied, so this does not establish the reported phonetic analysis.

search_audit.query: 医 医 矢 小篆 說文 矢亦聲 匸; site:dict.variants.moe.edu.tw/dictView.jsp 殹 医聲 yì 医; Unicode Unihan U+77E2 矢 kMandarin shǐ U+533B 医 yī; 医 醫 simplified character official standard simplified counterpart
search_audit.outcome: Opened and inspected the Shuowen, Taiwan MOE dictionary, and Taiwan CNS11643 pages. Both official Unicode Unihan character lookups returned inaccessible errors. Verified current component/host reading pair from supplied local exact rows and an official Taiwan reading record for 矢; local rows are not represented as external evidence.

gaps: No directly inspected dated early artifact form or dated earliest attestation for 医 or 醫 was obtained; graphic development and earliest sense chronology remain unresolved.

The Shuowen weapon-container account for 医 and its component analysis are not independently confirmed by an early glyph image. No independent source establishes the container’s ancient name or pronunciation, so a whole-graph phonetic loan explanation for medical 醫 is unsupported.

The cited small-Xu phonetic interpretation of 矢 in 医 remains disputed. Current Mandarin readings shǐ/yī are not evidence of the historical sound relation, and the available local Baxter–Sagart table has no exact row for 医.
Official Unicode Unihan records for U+77E2 and U+533B could not be opened. The local exact readings were checked but no external Unicode click-through is claimed.
The sources preserve divergent historical explanations for 殹 and 酉 in 醫; inspected material does not settle their original motivation or establish a dated semantic chain from weapons to medicine.
The search did not verify the dating or transmission of cited classical examples as earliest attestations.
